acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec amendment (requirement IDs, non-goals, failure modes, acceptance evidence, rollback) defines the declared string-keyed registry dialect and its configuration; lane requirements are accepted under the owner's standing auto-accept of 2026-10-11.
A change to one registered builder selects only the tests that pass its literal key, plus every caller with a non-literal key, which are flagged as unknowns; keys are never dropped silently.
A change to the registry file itself still selects every caller of the accessor.
The receipt shows the registry line and the call-site line for each selected test; focused and hostile tests plus sealed change evidence; GitHub #871 closed by the merged PR.
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#871 (2026-10-14). impact on a builder module registered in an exported object literal (e.g. registry.ts `'ctx:club_with_two_courses': new ClubWithTwoCourses()`) returns only the changed path, registry.ts as a reverse import and unknowns dynamic-dispatch-unresolved, and no tests, because every spec reaches the registry through a data-provider fixture that takes a string key (createTestData('ctx:...')). Import closure then selects nothing (unsafe) or every spec (152/152 in the reporter's case, where one spec uses the key). Proposal: a narrow declared dialect: registry = exported object literal whose values are `new X()` or `X` of an imported binding -> key->module edges; call sites = literal string argument to an adopter-declared accessor -> test->key edges; impact on the module returns tests using its key with evidence lines for the registry entry and the call site; fail closed: a non-literal key at any accessor call site or a computed registry key is an unknown and widens selection to every caller of that accessor; configuration in a profile entry naming the registry export and accessor methods.
title: impact: resolve literal string-keyed registries (key -> module) to the tests that pass the key (GitHub #871)
